source_text: Intravit igitur, secundum Apostolum, per unum hominem peccatum in hunc mundum et per peccatum mors, quoniam illum et reum et damnationi mortis perpetuae destinatum mundus aspexit. In omnes autem homines mors pertransiit, quia una forma iudicii praevaricatores quosque etiam reliquae comprehendit aetatis; quae tamen mors nec in sanctos nec in innocentes ullos saevire permittitur, sed in eos pervadit, quos praevaricationem viderit aemulatos [n95] .
pass_a_gloss: There entered therefore, according to the Apostle, through one human being sin into this world and through sin death, since the world looked at that man both a defendant and destined to the condemnation of perpetual death. But into all human beings death passed through, because one form of judgment comprehended also the transgressors of the remaining age; which death nevertheless is not permitted to rage either against the holy or against any innocents, but it invades those whom it has seen to have rivaled the transgression.

lemmas.lexica: LS praevaricatio; Blaise Adam's transgression as example
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5

pass_b_english: According to the apostle, then, sin entered this world through one man, and death through sin, because the world saw that man guilty and destined for condemnation to everlasting death (Romans 5:12). Death passed into all human beings because the same form of judgment encompasses transgressors in later ages too. Yet this death is not permitted to rage against any holy or innocent people: it invades those whom it finds imitating the transgression (compare Augustine, Proceedings of Pelagius 23.57).

choices.why: Adam's act of crossing the command; Julian's example of sin, not a transmitted nature.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
